newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira parity debate may delay ERM return - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Lira parity debate may delay ERM return - analysts.

text.p: Italy and its European partners are manoeuvring behind the scenes to get the lira central parity rate in Europe's ERM which best suits their purposes and this could delay re-entry, analysts said on Thursday.

As the first weekend looms in which the lira could conceivably return to the exchange rate mechanism (ERM) it left in a currency crisis four years ago, economists say the central parity is the main bone of contention.
"The sticking point is the attitude of the French as regards the central rate," said Gwyn Hacche at HSBC Markets in London. "It's down to negotiations between the French and the Italians."
Falling inflation shown by data released late on Thursday and the possibility of the Bank of Italy trimming interest rates adds a further dimension to the lira's fortunes.

In a Reuter survey on Wednesday, five out of 10 economists polled expected the lira to re-enter the currency grid by the end of November, with three seeing the possibility of it happening this weekend.

But an Italian newspaper report on Thursday speculated Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio wants re-entry after Italy's upper house (Senate) has passed the 1997 budget package, which is due by Christmas. Prime Minister Romano Prodi warned on Wednesday that entry negotiations may take time.
In addition, analysts say France is concerned about the level at which Italy wants to return.
Lorenzo Codogno, chief economist at Bank of America in Milan, said: "There have been signals in the last few days that negotiations with Italy's EU partners are still up in the air."

"It's probable that it will happen before the date of the (Dublin) summit so long as we don't see unbridgeable differences opening up," he said referring to a meeting of EU leaders set for December 13 and 14.
Dominic Konstam, economist at Credit Suisse First Boston in London, told Reuters Financial Television Italy's indication it wants 1,010 lira to the mark was seen as too weak for the French.
"The idea is perhaps there's a delay to allow the lira to strengthen in the meantime and perhaps try and encourage a slightly stronger central rate for the lira," he said.
The lira firmed past the 1,000 per mark level on Thursday, moving through the barrier after holding near 1,006 recently.

Currency market traders have speculated recently that the Bank of Italy has been keeping it weaker than 1,000 as it has further interest rate cuts in the offing and does not want a high rate prior to re-entry.
Konstam said delaying re-entry was a risky strategy. "The whole point of having an undervalued lira is that it allows interest rates to be lower than they would otherwise be."
Preliminary November Italian consumer prices data released late on Thursday showed Italian inflation was likely to be 2.6 percent year on year compared with 3.0 in October.

This fuelled some economists' expectations the Bank of Italy could cut the discount rate, now at 7.5 percent, a further 50 to 75 basis points soon. Trimming rates could affect lira strength and is therefore an ERM-sensitive action.

Hacche at HSBC said: "The question is whether you get a quick move on interest rates by the Bank of Italy to curb the rise in the lira or whether it holds on rates and lets the lira appreciate further."
